craft_notes: Color: mockery-turned-worship (anubhAva per NOTE). Firing: question kept open (mockery unexplained); bow answers mockery (poet sides with humble tree). Passive kept (tree stays center). REJECTED OPTIONS (with killers): (a) answering why -> killed: unexplained is the verse. (b) adverbial tone (fondly/cruelly) -> killed by BOUNDARY double-live. Read aloud: KU-ṭa-ja, WHY art-THOU LAUGHED-at BY-flow-ers … I-BOW — HARD in-DEED to-LAUGH at THEE. Abhinavagupta frame: grove as vibhāva, not backdrop — beauty as cause; kuṭaja-mockery and nīpa-release as anubhāva (consequents), not ornament; rasa overwhelming perception (dust obscuring sun/moon).

lines: Kuṭaja, why art thou laughed at by flowers?
I bow — hard indeed to laugh at thee.
l4.sanskrit_cite: kuṭaja kiṃ kusumair avahasyate praṇipatāmi ca duṣprahasya te

c1_essence: Beauty is not decoration but cause: the groves shine for Kāma's sake, not the reverse. The grove is the vibhāva (determinant) of śṛṅgāra; the rasa overwhelms perception — dust of passion obscures sun and moon, new-cloud-drunk peacocks cry. The kuṭaja's mockery and the nīpa's release are consequents (anubhāva), not ornament: the poet sides with the humble tree over showy flowers. The bee kisses the yūthikā creeper. The rasa is aesthetic: the rasa IS the point.
